notes: Chosen hook 'ANTHROPIC: 58% GOES TO COMPUTE'. Clarity 9 (two short lines, readable in under 2s on the cover). Curiosity 6 (the reader wonders what the rest goes to and why it matters; no tension beyond the figure). Concrete number or name 9 (Anthropic plus 58%, and 58% is yellow-highlighted). Promise kept 8 (slide 3 in the JSON states compute took 58% of revenue, up from 48%, and the slides go on to the $10B bill and the 1.72x chart; slide 2 gives the $17B context. The cover leaves out 'of revenue', so 'goes to' is a little loose, but the slides never contradict it, and it avoids calling 58% a margin or claiming a loss). Reader stake 3 (this is about the IPO filing and the company's finances; a reader will not expect a change for themselves). Stake is a plus, not a requirement, so the other four scores carry it. Overall 7. Options: #2 '$17B REVENUE, 58% TO COMPUTE' has two numbers but no company name, and its second line is the same claim, so it is weaker alone. #3 has no figure. #4 'REVENUE SOARS, COMPUTE SOARS' mixes revenue growth with a share of revenue, which is not like for like, as hook_pick_reason says. The chosen hook is the best option. Labels: #1 and #2 'number' are honest. #3 'claim' is fine. #4 'myth-flip' is not honest, because it states no myth and flips nothing; it is closer to a parallel claim or contrast. This is a note only, since #4 was not chosen. hook_pick_reason has an honest 'No reader-impact hook:' sentence (the article is about Anthropic's finances ahead of its IPO and states no effect on ordinary readers). Optional tweak: 'OF REVENUE' on the cover would tighten the promise, but the current wording passes.
